questions.q: At 27°C temperature, the mean kinetic energy of the atoms of an ideal gas is E$_1$. If this atomic temperature is increased to 327°C, then the mean kinetic energy of the atoms will be
questions.explanation: Mean KE $\propto T$(kelvin). $27^\circ C=300$K and $327^\circ C=600$K, so temperature doubles and mean KE becomes $2E_1$.

questions.q: The ratio of molar specific heats of oxygen is
questions.explanation: $\gamma = 1 + 2/f$; for a diatomic gas like O$_2$, $f=5$, so $\gamma = 1+2/5 = 1.4$.

questions.q: Pressure of ideal gas at constant volume is proportional to ____.
options: average potential energy of the molecules
average kinetic energy of the molecules
questions.explanation: From kinetic theory, PV = (2/3)E where E is the total translational kinetic energy of the gas molecules, so at constant V, P is proportional to the total energy of the gas.

questions.q: The speed of sound in an ideal gas at a given temperature T is v. The rms speed of gas molecules at that temperature is v$_{rms}$. The ratio of the velocities v and v$_{rms}$ for helium and oxygen gases are X and X' respectively. Then $\dfrac{X}{X'}$ is equal to
A gas mixture contains monoatomic and diatomic molecules of 2 moles each. The mixture has a total internal energy of (symbols have usual meanings)
Pressure of an ideal gas is increased by keeping temperature constant. The kinetic energy of molecules
options: Increases or decreases depending on the nature of gas
questions.explanation: Average kinetic energy of gas molecules depends only on the absolute temperature; since T is constant, KE remains unchanged.

questions.q: The mean energy of a molecule of an ideal gas is
questions.explanation: By the kinetic theory of gases, the mean translational kinetic energy per molecule is $\dfrac{3}{2}k_BT$.

questions.q: A perfect gas at $27^0C$ is heated at constant pressure so as to double its volume. The increase in temperature of the gas will be .....................
questions.explanation: At constant pressure, $V/T$ is constant; $T_1=300$ K, doubling $V$ doubles $T$ to 600 K $=327^0C$; the increase in temperature is $327-27=300^0C$.

questions.q: The temperature of a gas contained in a closed vessel of constant volume increases by 1$^0$C when the pressure of the gas is increased by 1%. The initial temperature of the gas is .....................
questions.explanation: At constant volume $P\propto T$: $\dfrac{1.01T}{T}=\dfrac{T+1}{T}\Rightarrow T=100$ K.
